result: Swap cost split per call (openat 17.8k, pread 3.7k, close 1.9k, mremap 33.1k kernel instr in-call on Broadwell-EP; +65.5k per start; N100 +29.3 us, +15.6%); floor proved above the 5k target (any call that can change page 0's mapping costs 20-31k on kernel 6.8); default stays off; D-4.53 amended
head: 2bcd8655

gate.affected: keke classed-slot-swap-cost-gate rc 0 on 2bcd8655: every step ok (liella, boundary, math, rt, both export modes; conformance 121 programs)

rulings.item: Replace the /proc/self/pagemap guard with a user-space int3 (0xcc) scan of both pages (2.05k user instr, 0 kernel; cuts ~48k kernel instr and ~16.7 us per start on the N100; changes #3140)
rulings.recommendation: only if the swap is ever wanted on; it still leaves +44-60k, so keep the default off and spend nothing more on the swap until a slot shows a measured per-call gain

informational: Any GLIBC_TUNABLES value costs Liella's static start-up +38k to +51k kernel instructions and +13.7 us on the N100 (+37 us Ivy Bridge); an unrelated env var costs nothing: worth its own story (profile first)
improvement: A per-call kernel-instruction probe (perf_event_open, exclude_user, around each syscall) settles start-up cost splits in seconds without perf trace; worth a tools/probe/ template
next_step: Coordinator rules on the guard scan; otherwise nothing, the swap stays off
